defects.description: Adversarial review, lens CODE-QUALITY, both passes completed. (1) Dead code/abstraction: none — every added symbol is used; parse_port remains a single flat function with no single-caller indirection, no forwarding wrappers, no unread parameters; the two local names (port) are immediately consumed. (2) Structure & clarity: parse_port does exactly one thing (validate-then-convert); the validation logic is not duplicated anywhere; the range bounds 1 and 65535 are magic literals but are the domain-defining TCP port limits named directly in the frozen intent and in the error message itself, so named constants would be over-abstraction for an 11-line module. The guard `not isinstance(text, str) or not text.isascii() or not text.isdigit()` is a three-clause compound condition — mildly dense but idiomatic and self-documenting via the error message; recorded as this cosmetic LOW nit only. Names (parse_port, port, text) are accurate; the docstring at parseport.py:5 was updated in lockstep with the new behavior, so no stale-comment drift. (3) Convention drift: Read of both full files confirms consistency — test_parseport.py keeps the pre-existing unittest.TestCase class layout, method naming style test_<verb>_<subject>, self.assertEqual/assertRaises idioms, and the __main__ unittest.main() footer; the new subTest loops in test_rejects_non_numeric_input/test_rejects_port_below_range/test_rejects_port_above_range are standard unittest idiom and match the file's style. Import style unchanged (single `from parseport import parse_port`). Error-handling idiom (raise ValueError with f-string messages) is uniform across both checks. Second pass (demanding-reviewer test): the change is minimal, reads like the surrounding code, and would be accepted without a rewrite. Deterministic evidence quality.lint_deliverable reported no defects, consistent with this review. No CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM findings; verdict OK.
